identity.name: Emirate of Bani Khalid
alt_names: Bani Khalid emirate of Eastern Arabia

land.text: Al-Hasa and Qatif, the Ottoman Al-Hasa Eyalet (Lahsa) set up in 1552

predecessors.note: The Eyalet page: 'The beglerbegilik of Al-Hasa was established in 1552'; the ottoman-empire dossier gives 1560 for its creation. In 1669-1670 Barrak ibn Ghurayr's Al-Humaid section of the Bani Khalid defeated the Ottoman garrison at al-Ahsa and the administration 'withdrew peacefully'.

land.text: Al-Hasa and Qatif, after 'a battle against the Subay' and the Al Saud' that 'ended the rule of the Bani Khalid' in 1830

successors.note: The page's 1830 date conflicts with its 1793 Saudi invasion and the 1818 Ottoman restoration; the Saudi interlude 1793-1818 is a gap in the dossier.

capitals.name: Al-Mubarraz
capitals.note: 'Capital: Al-Mubarraz, where remnants of his castle still stand' (Barrak's). The Eyalet page names Lahsa the largest town and administrative centre of the Ottoman period and has the Banu Khalid make Mubarraz their headquarters in the 1560 rebellion.

correction.text: Al-Hasa and Qatif, the land the Bani Khalid held after expelling the Ottomans in 1670

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the state; its Ottoman shape drew Hasa, Kuwait and Qatar until 1670 per the ottoman-empire dossier). The page's lead says the tribe ruled 'southern Iraq, Kuwait, and Eastern Arabia (al-Hasa and al-Qatif)' and 'the region of Najd', undated; Qatar and Bahrain are not named as dominions. Only Al-Hasa and Qatif are drawn, as two discs (about 20,700 km2 by cells): the page gives no area. Saudi attacks began in 1789 (the Saud page) and the Saudi invasion that deposed the Al 'Uray'ir is dated 1793 on this page, so the frame runs to 1792.

correction.text: Al-Hasa and Qatif, restored when the Ottomans 'reinstated the Al 'Uray'ir as rulers' in 1818

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. '1818: the Ottomans overthrew the Al Saud, conquered al-Hasa and al-Qatif, and reinstated the Al 'Uray'ir as rulers'; the Bani Khalid 'were no longer a major military force' and lost a battle in 1823 to an alliance led by the Mutayr and 'Ajman. The pages give no month.

ledger.note: 1670: Barrak ibn Ghurayr founds the emirate. The Al-Humaid section of the Bani Khalid 'expelled Ottoman forces from the cities and towns in 1670 and proclaimed their rule over the region'; the Eyalet page has them defeating the Ottoman garrison at al-Ahsa in 1669-1670, after which the administration 'withdrew peacefully', and setting up 'an independent state, the Bani Khalid Emirate, in 1670'.

1789: Saud ibn Abd al-Aziz attacks Al-Hasa. 'Saud led the forces of the Emirate in 1789 and conquered Al Hasa region', defeating the Bani Khalid army; he 'won a victory eliminating the dominance of Bani Khalid in the region in 1792'. The Bani Khalid page dates the Saudi invasion that deposed the Al 'Ura'yir to 1793. The page says the Emirate of Diriyah 'could not completely capture the eastern Arabia' (undated).
1793: the contest ends with the Saudi invasion of al-Hasa. 'The Saudis invaded al-Hasa and deposed the Al 'Ura'yir.' No month on the page.

1793: Al-Hasa and Qatif pass to the Saudis. The Saud page's 1792 'elimination of the dominance of Bani Khalid' and the 1789 conquest differ by up to four years from the 1793 of the Bani Khalid page; the Diriyah dossier's own pages give 1794 for Qatif and 1795 for Hasa. 1793 is the date the Bani Khalid page gives for the deposition of the ruling house.

1818: the Ottomans restore the Al 'Uray'ir. 'The Ottomans overthrew the Al Saud, conquered al-Hasa and al-Qatif, and reinstated the Al 'Uray'ir as rulers.' The page gives no month; the Egyptian-Ottoman army took Diriyah in September 1818 (muhammad-ali-dynasty dossier).

1830: the rule ends. 'A battle against the Subay' and the Al Saud ended the rule of the Bani Khalid'; in 1823 the Bani Khalid had lost a battle to an alliance led by the Mutayr and 'Ajman, the year the Al Saud re-established their rule in Riyadh. The Ottomans appointed a Bani Khalid governor over al-Hasa again in 1874, briefly (outside the dossier's life).

wars.name: Saudi conquest of Al-Hasa
wars.outcome: 1789 Saud led the forces of the Emirate and conquered Al Hasa; 1792 'victory eliminating the dominance of Bani Khalid'; 1793 the Saudis deposed the Al 'Ura'yir (Bani Khalid page); the Bani Khalid had tried to invade Nejd and Diriyah, and failed.
wars.note: The Bani Khalid page dates the invasion to 1793; the Saud page gives 1789 and 1792.

wars.name: Ottoman restoration in Al-Hasa
wars.outcome: 1818: the Ottomans overthrew the Al Saud, conquered al-Hasa and al-Qatif and reinstated the Al 'Uray'ir as rulers.
wars.note: The war article was not opened.

certainty.note: A tribal emirate with no described boundary on the pages opened: Al-Hasa and Qatif are firm; the broader claim of the lead (southern Iraq, Kuwait, Najd) is undated and not drawn; the discs are the researcher's.

sources.title: Bani Khalid
sources.note: 1670 founding by Barrak ibn Ghurayr; capital Al-Mubarraz; 1793 Saudi invasion; 1818 Ottoman restoration; 1823 defeat by the Mutayr and Ajman; 1830 end; 1874 brief Ottoman appointment. Page silent on reign years and on Qatar, Bahrain.

sources.title: Eyalet of Al-Hasa
sources.note: The Ottoman eyalet of 1552, with Lahsa as its chief town; the 1669-1670 defeat of the garrison by Barrak ibn Ghurayr; the independent state set up in 1670.

sources.title: Saud bin Abdulaziz bin Muhammad Al Saud
sources.note: 1789 conquest of Al Hasa; the 1792 elimination of Bani Khalid dominance; the Emirate could not completely capture eastern Arabia.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks (its Ottoman Empire shape draws Hasa to 1670 per the ottoman-empire dossier). Slug emirate-of-bani-khalid is slugify of the title; the flagged variants bani-khalid (me-10-a) and bani-khalid-emirate (me-10-c) mean the same state; emirate-of-diriyah already uses the string 'Bani Khalid Emirate' as counterpart for its 1789-1795 events (contest_start 1789, gains 1794 Qatif and 1795 Hasa). Written by me-10-x; 3 pages opened (budget up to 5), a fourth (Emirate of Diriyah) was opened and is silent on Hasa. Titles that did not load: Emirate_of_Bani_Khalid, Emirate_of_Al-Hasa. The pages disagree on the end of the Saudi conquest (1792 on the Saud page, 1793 on the Bani Khalid page, 1794/1795 in the Diriyah dossier from other pages) and on the end of the emirate (1830 against 1793); the Bani Khalid page's 1818 restoration has no support for the Saudi-held years in between except the 1793 deposition, so 1793-1818 is left as a gap, and the Saudi years are drawn by emirate-of-diriyah. No rulers listed: the page gives none with reign years (Barrak ibn Ghurayr founded; Haddori is called the first chieftain of the Khawalid). The broader lead (southern Iraq, Kuwait, Najd) is not drawn; no page dates it. The Eyalet page gives 1552 for the eyalet's creation, the ottoman-empire dossier 1560. The Bani Khalid page also says that the Jabrids ruled Najd in the 15th and 16th centuries.
